However, you idx_9f4ed7d8 cannot change the instance family, operating system, or tenancy model.
If your requirements change, you can sell Standard Reserved Instances on the AWS
Reserved Instance Marketplace, provided idx_92a89d27 you meet the eligibility criteria. This
marketplace allows you to sell unused Standard Reserved Instances to other AWS
customers. You can sell your Reserved Instances when you no longer require those
instances, at the end of a project, or if your business requirements change.
Convertible Reserved Instance: This option offers greater flexibility at a lower
discount than idx_4c15f7a6 Standard Reserved Instances. With Convertible Reserved Instances, you
can exchange your idx_8db7ff90 instance for another Convertible Reserved Instance with a different:
Instance family
Operating system
Tenancy model
However, unlike Standard Reserved Instances, Convertible Reserved Instances cannot
be sold on the AWS Marketplace.
The amount you idx_9f183db9 pay upfront is a key factor in obtaining the maximum discount for Reserved
Instances. AWS offers three payment options to suit different budgeting needs. An example of a
standard 3-year reserved instance pricing option for a t2.micro Amazon Linux-based instance
is displayed in the following screenshot in Figure 8.4:
Figure 8.4: Reserved instance pricing options for a 3-year Amazon Linux t2.micro instance
With the All upfront option, you pay the total cost of the 1-year or 3-year term in advance at
the contract's start. This eliminates monthly or hourly billing, providing the most significant
possible discount, depending on the tenure of the contract. In Figure 8.4, you will note that the
effective rate for selecting this option is $0.004 per hour, which is the cheapest of all other
options.
The Partial upfront option allows you to pay a portion of the total cost at the beginning of the
contract, with the remainder billed monthly at a discounted rate. This approach helps reduce
monthly expenses while still offering substantial savings.
If you prefer not to make any upfront payments, the No upfront option lets you pay monthly at
a discounted hourly rate throughout the contract term. While this still offers savings compared

to On-Demand pricing, the discount is lower than what you would receive with All upfront or
Partial upfront payments.
You will also idx_a73df357 note an offer from a third-party provider, possibly another AWS customer
reselling a Standard Reserved Instance with a 27-month remaining contract.
Another pricing option offered by AWS is the Spot Instance Pricing Option, which is discussed
next.
Spot instance pricing options
AWS frequently has idx_0c33b1b9 excess compute capacity, aiming to sell it to maximize economies of scale.

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 8 218
chunks.content:
Customers occasionally idx_9fb5f2b8 require additional capacity, often for stateless workloads such as ad-
hoc batch jobs, extract, transform, and load (ETL) operations, or media processing. AWS
offers Spot Instances specifically idx_62e57184 designed for temporary and flexible workloads to encourage
the use of this surplus capacity.
AWS Spot Instances provide the most significant cost savings, offering discounts of up to 90%
off the On-Demand price. AWS determines the Spot Instance price based on current supply
and demand, which fluctuate over time. As a customer, you can specify a maximum price at or
above the prevailing Spot price when requesting a Spot Instance. Typically, you would set your
maximum price slightly above the current Spot price to account for minor fluctuations,
ensuring continued access to the instance. However, you are always charged at the prevailing
Spot price. If the Spot price rises above your specified maximum price, AWS will terminate
your instance with a minimum two-minute warning, as other customers may be willing to pay
the higher price for the available capacity.
Amazon EC2 generates an instance rebalance recommendation signal to alert you when a Spot
Instance is more likely to be interrupted. This notification allows you to proactively
redistribute your workloads across other existing or newly launched Spot Instances rather
than waiting for the idx_01abac26 standard two-minute interruption notice.
When you launch idx_8210ca31 EC2 instances, you are deploying virtual servers on shared physical
hardware by default. This means the host machine on which your EC2 instance is deployed
shares hardware resources with other EC2 instances that might belong to other customers.
While firewall configurations prevent you from accessing compute resources that belong to
other customers and vice versa, you may have a regulatory requirement to ensure that all your
virtual servers are deployed on a physical host consisting of instances that belong only to you.
The next section explains Dedicated Hosts, which is a pricing option that fulfills this
requirement.

chunks.heading: Chapter 8 220
chunks.content:
Chapter 8 220
Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts and Dedicated Instances
Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts provide idx_71808cdc a fully dedicated physical server exclusively for your
use. This ensures that the underlying hardware is isolated from other AWS customers while
still allowing you to share instance capacity across multiple AWS accounts. Dedicated Hosts
offer complete control and visibility over instance placement on the host, along with host
affinity, which ensures that workloads remain on the same physical machine. It also means
that you idx_a0f35fba can bring your own licenses (BYOL) to the platform. This is particularly beneficial
for software that requires licensing on a per-socket, per-core, or per-VM basis. Many
enterprise-grade applications have strict licensing conditions tied to the physical
infrastructure, making Dedicated Hosts an ideal solution. Billing is based on the host,
irrespective of the number of instances running on it.
Amazon EC2 Dedicated Instances is a similar offering to Dedicated Hosts except that the
physical host is dedicated to a single idx_46a593a3 AWS account, and you cannot share instance capacity
with other accounts. You also do not have visibility into sockets and cores, and cannot have
host affinity for your instances. There is only partial support for BYOL, specifically Microsoft
SQL Server with idx_0fbb0086 License Mobility through Software Assurance, and Windows Virtual Desktop
Access (VDA) licenses. However, dedicated instances fulfill the requirement of workloads
needing isolated hardware, which is particularly useful for highly regulated environments.
Amazon EC2 is a fundamental compute service in AWS that enables you to deploy virtual
machines in the cloud. It offers extensive flexibility, allowing you to configure instances with
various operating systems, networking features, storage options, and data transfer settings.
However, if you require a straightforward virtual server to run idx_9050b6ec standard off-the-shelf (OTS)
software with predictable monthly pricing, Amazon Lightsail provides a simpler alternative.
The next section will cover Amazon Lightsail in more detail.
Deploying simple workloads with Amazon Lightsail
Amazon Lightsail idx_5268a86e provides preconfigured Linux and Windows virtual servers in the cloud,
enabling customers to launch and manage common web applications quickly. Designed for
simplicity and ease of use, Lightsail automatically configures networking, access, and security
settings according to AWS best practices.
While configuration idx_9c989cd2 options are limited, Lightsail offers the advantage idx_59bbe434 of a predictable, fixed
monthly pricing model based on instance type, operating system, and bundled applications. It
is well-suited for small business applications such as file storage, accounting software, simple

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 8 220
chunks.content:
web applications running on WordPress or Magento, and LAMP stack deployments.
Additionally, Lightsail is an excellent option for managed service providers and resellers who
need a hassle-free hosting solution without the complexity of hardware management.
221 AWS Compute Services – EC2, Lightsail, ECS, EKS, and Lambda
Although virtual machines have significantly shaped modern cloud computing, they have
limitations. Each virtual machine requires its own guest operating system, consuming
additional resources. To address this challenge, AWS offers container-based compute
solutions, which provide a more efficient and scalable alternative. The concept of
containerization is explored in the next section.
Running containers with Amazon ECS and Amazon
EKS
Traditional virtual machines (VMs) are idx_1495b83a deployed on bare-metal hardware configured with a
hypervisor. The hypervisor abstracts and manages physical resources such as CPU, memory,
and storage, enabling multiple VMs to run on the same hardware. Each VM functions
independently, requiring its own operating system, libraries, and runtime environments to
support its applications.
Due to compatibility requirements, multiple idx_0aff7ec1 VMs are often deployed to host different
application environments. For example, as illustrated in Figure 8.5, a development VM may
have the latest software versions for building new features, applications, or experimentation.
In contrast, a production VM may need to run an older, stable version. Multiple VMs must be
provisioned for each environment to avoid compatibility issues and ensure isolation.
Figure 8.5: VMs hosting different versions of software for various environments

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 8 222
chunks.content:
Chapter 8 222
Each VM also includes its own guest operating system (Windows or Linux), which must be
patched, managed, and monitored. This increases administrative overhead and leads to higher
resource consumption.
Containerization idx_a2acf30f is a more efficient and agile approach to provisioning compute capacity. This
technology enables applications to run in isolated user spaces, known as containers, which
share the same underlying operating system. Containers package all necessary dependencies,
including binaries, libraries, configuration files, and runtime environments, ensuring
consistency across different environments.
Since containers are abstracted from the host operating system while maintaining secure,
isolated access, they allow for significantly higher density than traditional VMs. As illustrated
in Figure 8.6, this results in more efficient resource utilization and improved scalability.
Figure 8.6: Containers running on the Docker engine
You would use a container engine to manage containers, and Docker is one of the world's most
popular technologies for building, deploying, and managing containers.
Containerization idx_ee45fcbd significantly reduces overhead by allowing multiple containers to share the
same underlying host operating system, rather than requiring each instance to have its own
kernel, as with virtual machines.
223 AWS Compute Services – EC2, Lightsail, ECS, EKS, and Lambda
As illustrated in Figure 8.6, containers leverage a container runtime, such as the Docker engine,
to access the host OS while maintaining isolation. This eliminates the need for full guest
operating systems, making the application footprint much smaller than VMs. As a result,
containerized applications benefit from improved performance, faster startup times, and more
efficient resource utilization than traditional VM-based architectures.
AWS offers two fully idx_a7783291 managed container orchestration services that allow you to deploy
Docker-style applications – Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) and Amazon Elastic
Kubernetes Service (EKS). These idx_e5bb7e56 two services are discussed next.
Overview of Amazon Elastic Container Service
Amazon ECS is a idx_cbf88b13 fully managed container orchestration service that enables you to deploy,
manage, and scale containerized applications. With Amazon ECS, you do not need to install
and operate your own container orchestration software or manage and scale clusters of virtual
machines. The service offers all these capabilities as a fully managed service, enabling you to
focus on building and deploying your container images.
As part of the service, AWS idx_858bae94 also offers the Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR), a fully
managed container image registry service. With seamless integration to Amazon ECS, you can

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 8 222
chunks.content:
build and manage all your container images, define their access permissions and deploy those
images as containers on Amazon ECS.
Amazon ECS offers two idx_ab6a1d95 deployment options:
Amazon Fargate (Fargate launch type): This option is serverless because you do not
need to manage idx_4eacc403 any underlying EC2 instances to host your containers. You package
your application, specify the CPU, memory, and networking parameters, and AWS
provisions the necessary container infrastructure within a secure, isolated
environment accessible only via your VPC. AWS automatically places ECS tasks on the
cluster, scales them as needed, and fully manages the underlying environment.
EC2 launch type: This option idx_a7b406ba allows you to manage a cluster of EC2 instances and
manually schedule the placement of containers. You have complete control over the
underlying instances, including the ability to patch, update, and optimize their
configurations.
Amazon ECS Managed Instances: This idx_4b2d1a48 option allows you to run containers on EC2
instances while letting AWS handle much of the infrastructure management for you.
AWS manages tasks such as instance provisioning, patching, and capacity
management, while you still retain control over the type of instances used for your
workloads. This is useful when you want more control than Fargate provides, such as
•
•
•

chunks.content:
Chapter 8 224
choosing GPU-optimized or network-optimized instances, but do not want to manage
every aspect of the underlying EC2 fleet yourself.
Choosing between ECS launch options:
The EC2 launch type is best suited for long-running applications that require manual
auto-scaling management or cost optimizations through Reserved Instances
The Fargate launch type is ideal for periodic or unpredictable workloads, offering on-
demand scaling and minimal administrative overhead since AWS handles
infrastructure management
Amazon ECS Managed Instances is probably the best of both worlds in that AWS
manages the instances, such as patching, capacity provision, workload placements, but idx_11d2eb61
you still get to choose the configuration like instance types, GPU and network
optimized instances as well as access reserved capacity
In the next section, you will learn about the Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service.
Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
Kubernetes is an idx_28f02365 open-source and vendor-agnostic container orchestration service. Like ECS, it
offers container orchestration, scaling, and management of applications across clusters of
machines. Amazon EKS is AWS's offering of the Kubernetes service, which comes with existing
tooling and plugins from partners and the Kubernetes community. This means you can also
easily migrate existing Kubernetes clusters to AWS. Note that with EKS, you need to pay for the
control plane, but there is no additional charge for ECS.
While containerization improves resource efficiency and performance, AWS also offers another
compute service called AWS Lambda. This serverless compute solution executes code in
response to events or triggers, enabling the development of event-driven architectures.
Serverless computing with AWS Lambda is explored in the next section.
Building event-driven applications with AWS Lambda
AWS Lambda idx_d2d33c20 is a serverless compute offering that allows you to run code in response to an
event or a trigger. Also known idx_95bd4f33 as Function as a Service (FaaS), AWS Lambda functions can be
invoked to run code and be architected as part of your serverless architecture, including other
technologies such as storage, databases, and network connectivity.
Depending idx_e20be57b on your application type and architecture, you idx_fe92f12f can handle all compute and
processing tasks using Lambda functions rather than spin up EC2 instances to perform any
computational work or process data. There are limitations, however, to consider, but it is
possible to build a complete end-to-end application using Lambda to handle the compute
layer.
•
•
•
225 AWS Compute Services – EC2, Lightsail, ECS, EKS, and Lambda
The following architecture, shown in Figure 8.7, illustrates how AWS Lambda could be used to

chunks.heading: Chapter 8 224
chunks.content:
build a complete web application solution.
Figure 8.7: AWS serverless architecture with AWS Lambda
As shown in Figure 8.7, AWS Lambda provides compute services in response to events
representing state changes. The architecture is structured as follows:
The client visits a website hosted on an Amazon S3 bucket configured with static
website hosting. The example shown in the diagram is that of an e-commerce front-
end user interface (UI).
Amazon API Gateway enables developers to easily create, publish, and manage APIs.
The application would call specific APIs, such as GET or PUT, when retrieving product
lists or adding products to the cart, respectively.
API Gateway would then trigger the relevant AWS Lambda function. In this example,
when users request to view their shopping cart, as illustrated in Figure 8.7, the Lambda
function executes code to retrieve the relevant data from the backend database.
Amazon DynamoDB hosts the web application's backend data, including customer
information, product details, and order records. DynamoDB is ideal for storing large
volumes of unstructured data and does not require extensive prior schema
configurations. Chapter 9 explores DynamoDB in greater detail.
AWS Lambda functions idx_eddc0058 are executed when triggered or idx_a105b498 invoked by another AWS service and
do not run independently. This means their use cases are based on event-driven architectures,
which may also include scheduled events.
AWS Lambda is designed for short-running tasks rather than prolonged backend processing.
As such, there are certain limitations on where Lambda functions can be used. For example, a
Lambda function can run for 15 minutes per invocation, and a single function can use up to
10,240 MB of memory. In most cases, simple web requests such as retrieving a list of products
from an e-commerce website take no more than 1 second, and so the 15-minute timeout limit is
plenty for such use cases. The best part about Lambda is that you only pay when your code
executes. This is much more cost-effective than EC2 instances, which often run idle as you wait
for events to occur.

chunks.content:
Chapter 8 226
So far, this chapter has focused extensively on hosting applications in the cloud – using a wide
range of compute services, including virtual machines with Amazon EC2, containerization
with Amazon ECS and EKS, and serverless event-driven compute offerings such as AWS
Lambda. However, many organizations may wish to bring cloud resources to their on-premises
environment – this may be because of compliance and governance reasons or technical
requirements such as having ultra-low latency access to these resources. The next section
introduces AWS Outpost, which offers a solution to this requirement.
Extending AWS compute to on-premises
environments with AWS Outposts
AWS Outposts allow idx_085e5ad6 customers to deploy cloud resources such as EC2 instances, S3 storage,
and RDS databases on-premises. These resources run on AWS-supplied physical infrastructure,
which includes racks, servers, storage, and networking equipment. All resources are managed
using the same AWS management tools and services as in the cloud.
The physical infrastructure consists of a 42U rack, 48 inches deep, capable of housing 1U or 2U
servers where your resources are provisioned. From a connectivity perspective, AWS Outposts
extend your Amazon VPC from the AWS Region to your on-premises environment by defining
"Outpost subnets." These subnets provide access to VPC components such as internet
gateways, endpoints, and transit gateways. An Outpost acts as an extension of an Availability
Zone in the associated Region, allowing you to benefit from its high availability and resilience.
In the next section, you will launch some EC2 instances, configure connectivity, and access
those instances to remotely administer them.
Project task 8 – Deploying EC2 instances in public
and private subnets of your VPC
In the upcoming project idx_5ebb1cd6 tasks, you will learn how to deploy and administer Linux-based EC2
instances within the VPC you created in Chapter 7. You will launch one instance in the public
subnet and one in the private, as depicted in Figure 8.8:

The EC2 instance in the public subnet will require a public IP address and act as a
Bastion Host - A bastion host is a server used to securely access and manage resources
in a private subnet by acting as a gateway for administrative tasks, typically via SSH or
RDP. To ensure connectivity to the server, you will also create a new security group that
will allow inbound traffic on port 22 for SSH from the Internet. Think of the bastion

Once you connect to this bastion host, you will then be able to access the EC2 instance

Summary
In this chapter, you explored a variety of AWS compute services, beginning with Amazon EC2,
AWS's core virtual server offering. You learned about Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), which
serve as templates that include the operating system, necessary software, and current patch
levels—allowing you to launch EC2 instances as fully functional servers. You discovered that
AMIs are available through Quick Start, the AWS Community, and the Marketplace, and that
you can also build custom AMIs to meet your organization's specific needs.
You also examined the different EC2 instance types and families, understanding how each type
corresponds to hardware characteristics like CPU, memory, and networking performance. Your
learning continued with an overview of EC2 storage options such as Amazon EBS, Amazon
EFS, and Amazon FSx, helping you understand how to attach persistent storage to your
instances.
Additionally, you looked at the range of EC2 pricing models and learned how to select the most
cost-effective option for your applications. Depending on your workload's requirements, you
explored how to take advantage of discounted pricing options like Reserved Instances, Spot
Instances, and Dedicated Hosts.
To wrap up, you were introduced to other AWS compute services beyond EC2. You considered
the advantages of using containers for application deployment and learned that using
serverless solutions like AWS Lambda to build event-driven architectures is best.
In the following chapter, we will move from the compute layer to the data layer, learning how
AWS database services store, protect, scale, and migrate the data that those applications
depend on.

Databases on AWS
At the heart of most applications, you will need to store, organize, analyze, and manipulate
data in some form or another. Most applications will have a data store component where
application-related data is hosted, and often you would use a database for this. This database is
designed to help you organize data in a manner that makes it possible to derive information
that consumers of your application require. For example, an e-commerce store will have a
database component that stores a customer's previous orders, allowing you to use cutting-
edge artificial intelligence and machine learning tools to build a personalized application that
can make intelligent recommendations for future purchases. Critical to offering any of these
functionalities is the raw data that needs to be stored in a manner that can be easily consumed.
In this chapter, you will learn the basics of databases, compare relational databases and non-
relational databases, and their appropriate use cases. In addition, you will learn about certain
industry-specific database solutions and get a thorough grounding in the architectural design
patterns, best practices, and security strategies when hosting sensitive and critical corporate
information. The topics covered in this chapter include:
Understanding database concepts and models
Working with relational databases on AWS
Securing database credentials with AWS Secrets Manager
Using Amazon DynamoDB for NoSQL workloads
Improving database performance with Amazon ElastiCache
Building data warehousing solutions with Amazon Redshift
Migrating databases with AWS Database Migration Service
•
•
•
•
•
•

Understanding database concepts and models
There are several idx_0e3fd0a3 database types and models, catering to the wide range of different
application requirements, such as the need for extensive complex queries or ultra-low latency,
through to databases that must support complex entity relationships and the more modern
vector-style databases to support artificial intelligence (AI) applications.
Perhaps one of the most common database models is the relational database, often referred to
as SQL-based databases. Relational databases are often compared to a spreadsheet – the
storage of structured data in a table, where rows define individual database records and
columns represent the attributes that provide specific details or properties of each record, such

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 8 240
chunks.content:
as name, age, or email address, in a typical customer database. The following diagram in Figure
9.1 depicts a typical table that stores customer details for an e-commerce company.
Figure 9.1: Customer contact table
As depicted in Figure 9.1, the Customer Contact Details table contains multiple records, each
providing a specific customer's address information. The columns represent individual pieces
of data that collectively offer meaningful insight into a customer's physical address.
A primary key is a crucial idx_60a59cb1 column in any relational database. A primary key is an attribute that
holds a unique value for every record, enabling you to identify each one uniquely—no two
records can share the same primary key. In this table, the primary key is labeled as
CustomerID —a unique string that is not repeated elsewhere in the table. For example, you
can easily identify Holly McDonald by using the CustomerID ' CS7002 ' in a query to retrieve
her address details.
Another key feature of relational databases is the ability to have multiple tables, each storing a
specific set of data that can be linked to other tables through joins. This design enables the
creation of a highly efficient and scalable database architecture.

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 244
chunks.content:
Chapter 9 244
For example, in Figure 9.1, the Customer Contact Details table contains information about
customers and their contact details, including their home addresses. Now, imagine if each
customer's order information were included in the same table. This approach would lead to
inefficiencies due to data duplication, such as repeating the address details for every order a
customer places.
An example of what this might look like is shown in Figure 9.2:
Figure 9.2: Duplicate data example
As illustrated, the idx_c47a6dd9 contact details for Bob Smith are repeated for each order he placed. This
repetition is highly inefficient and results in unnecessary use of storage and system resources.
Instead, by leveraging the ability to host multiple tables, each focused on a specific area of the
overall data set, you can achieve greater efficiency and improved data management. These
tables can then be idx_652ffd1b joined using primary keys and foreign keys, allowing queries to be
idx_0863e138 executed more efficiently.
For example, in Figure 9.3, you'll notice there are two tables: one for Customer Contact Details
and another for Orders placed by customers. The Orders table has its unique primary key, called
OrderID. It also includes a column that links each order back to the customer who placed it—
this is known as the foreign key.
245 Databases on AWS
Figure 9.3: Join between the customer order table and the customer contact table
The example idx_a05e8b3b illustrated in Figure 9.3 shows that Alice Brown has placed three orders. Rather
than using a single table with extensive data duplication, you can structure the database using
multiple related tables connected through joins. This approach allows you to reference data in
one table from another without repeating the same information.
In this example, there's no need to duplicate Alice's contact details for each order she places.
Instead, by mapping the OrderID in the Orders table to the CustomerID in the Customer
Contact table, you can easily identify who placed each order. This structure enables more
efficient queries and ensures data consistency.
In the Orders table, the column CustomerID acts as a foreign key, linking back to the primary
key in the Customer Contact Details table.
You can then run queries across your tables to retrieve all the necessary related information.
For example, if you want to generate a statement of account, you can query the order details for
a specific customer and list them in the statement. At the same time, you can retrieve the
customer's contact details to complete the statement, making it ready to be sent to the
customer.
The term relational in relational database refers to the concept of relations, which in database
theory are essentially tables.
Each table (relation) stores data about a specific entity, such as Customers or Orders •

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 246
chunks.content:
Chapter 9 246
These tables are related to each other using keys:
Primary keys uniquely identify records in a table
Foreign keys establish relationships between different tables
You can query across multiple tables using joins, thanks to these relationships
To query relational idx_48769643 databases, you use a special language called a structured query language,
or SQL for short. SQL is used to interact with databases, enabling you to idx_5b540c18 create tables and
relationships, insert, update, and delete data in tables, and run queries across multiple tables.
Typical databases that utilize the SQL language include MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and
Oracle.
Relational databases are also idx_1b702a49 referred to as Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) databases.
This type of database is designed for transactional workloads, which involve frequently
adding, updating, and deleting small amounts of data. A common term idx_6cc88dda used in this context is
CRUD, which stands for Create, Read, Update, and Delete.
Relational idx_0dc197be databases, or Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS), perform
these CRUD operations in response to requests from your applications. Examples of
transactional applications include an e-commerce website that processes customer orders or
an employee database used by an HR application.
In the next section, you idx_ef349b0a will learn more about Relational Databases on AWS.
Working with relational databases on AWS
Relational idx_7374818a databases, such as MySQL or Microsoft SQL idx_0265d443 Server, must run on a compute resource,
such as an Amazon EC2 instance. You need to install the database engine, after which you can
interact with it idx_8a50768e using idx_893737e9 either a command-line interface (CLI) or a graphical user interface
(GUI).
It's important to understand that a relational database requires core infrastructure
components—compute, storage, and network connectivity—to be accessible and usable by
your applications.
While installing and configuring a database engine like MySQL or Oracle on an EC2 instance is
a valid approach, AWS offers a fully managed solution called Amazon Relational Database
Service (Amazon RDS). Amazon idx_086dd37d RDS is an OLTP database designed for transaction-based
workloads, such as student enrolment applications for universities or databases used in e-
commerce applications. As another example related to the client requirements of Belly Brew
Co. Limited, Amazon RDS can be used to host stock inventory data for its gut-friendly
beverages, which will be updated regularly as orders are fulfilled and stock is replenished.
•
◦
◦
•
247 Databases on AWS
The key difference is that with Amazon RDS, you do not need to manage the underlying virtual
machines or infrastructure that host the database engine—AWS handles it for you.

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 246
chunks.content:
With EC2 self-hosting, AWS only manages the underlying physical host layer and the
hypervisor software. You are responsible for managing, configuring, and securing the EC2
instances on which you install your chosen database engine. The following diagram in Figure
9.4 illustrates the key differences idx_d597ecf5 between hosting your own database idx_925cb552 engine on EC2 instances
vs. using the Amazon RDS service.
Figure 9.4: Self-hosted on EC2 vs. Amazon RDS
With Amazon RDS, AWS handles the administrative burden of installing, configuring,
patching, and upgrading the database. This is achieved by abstracting away the underlying
database administration tasks.
You still retain control over how the database is configured—such as the amount of CPU and
memory allocated or how much storage is provisioned—by making API calls via the AWS
Management Console or CLI.
You simply select the desired instance type and storage options, and AWS provisions the
required resources for you.

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 248
chunks.content:
Chapter 9 248
Additionally, you can access the database using client tools or your application via AWS SDKs
(Software Development Kits). However, you do not have access to the underlying operating
system or the software components of the database engine that AWS provisions.
Amazon RDS offers several database engines that suit a wide range of businesses and enable
companies to easily migrate their workloads to the cloud. These are:
MySQL
PostgreSQL
Microsoft SQL
Oracle

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: IBM DB2
chunks.content:
IBM DB2
Amazon also offers its proprietary database, which is Amazon Aurora. This database offering
comes with idx_fa521c0d unparalleled high performance and availability, and has three idx_12c5b2dc variants
(compatibility): Aurora for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DSQL.
In the next section, you will learn about the core features of Amazon RDS.
Amazon RDS compute and storage options
To deploy a database idx_f65b4140 using the Amazon RDS service, you must launch an RDS instance with
your chosen engine. This instance runs on compute resources solely managed by AWS, and you
do not have access to the underlying operating system or the database application software.
Once your database instance has been provisioned, you can use client tools and utilities, or
application code, to connect to the database instance and create one or more databases. Within
each database, you can create one or more tables according to your application requirements.
To provision your Amazon RDS database, you must select an instance configuration from the
available options. AWS offers three different classes to choose from – each with a range of
various instance types that define the amount of CPU, memory, and other features, such as
optimized writes and idx_6ceb5a6f network bandwidth.
These include the following:
Standard classes (including the m classes): designed for a balance of compute,
memory, and network resources, and ideal for most modern applications
Memory-optimized classes (including the r and x classes): designed for the most
demanding applications, which require increased memory and are optimized for
memory-intensive applications
Burstable classes (includes t classes): designed for non-production workloads and
offer baseline performance levels with the ability to burst to full CPU usage during
occasional spikes in demand
•

249 Databases on AWS
The following screenshot in Figure 9.5 illustrates the available instance classes to choose from
when provisioning your database instance.
Figure 9.5: Instance configuration options
Once you select the idx_39715bcc class, you can then choose the appropriate instance size from the drop-
down menu – this provides a selection of types offering varying levels of CPU, memory, and
additional features, such as high-bandwidth networking, where applicable.
In addition to compute capacity, you must allocate storage for your database. AWS stores RDS
database idx_93c3bdee data on Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes. You can modify the allocated
storage capacity independently of the database instance class, allowing you to increase storage
without changing the compute resources assigned to the database. This allows you to increase
storage capacity without changing the instance type. The volume's throughput and IOPS
(input/output operations per second) depend on the type of EBS volume you provision. These

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: IBM DB2
chunks.content:
include:
General Purpose SSD (gp2/gp3): Ideal for most database workloads that do not
require extremely high IOPS. General-purpose SSD volumes support between 20 GiB
and 64 TiB of storage for MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. For Microsoft SQL Server
and Oracle, the range is 20 GiB to 16 TiB.
gp2 volumes provide performance based on the size of the volume, delivering a
baseline of 3 IOPS per GiB and allowing smaller volumes to burst performance
when additional throughput is required.
•
◦

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 250
chunks.content:
Chapter 9 250
gp3 volumes provide a baseline of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s throughput, with
the ability to provision additional IOPS and throughput independently of storage
capacity. This allows you to optimize performance without increasing storage
size.
Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2): Ideal for production-grade applications that require
fast and consistent I/O performance. With Provisioned IOPS SSDS, you specify both the
IOPS rate and the volume size, up to 64 Tib, depending on the database engine.
Amazon Aurora, however, offers idx_8e07c94b significantly idx_d9a60305 higher limits and capabilities, which will be
discussed later in this chapter.
The best part is that you can scale your storage as needed, and Amazon RDS also offers storage
autoscaling, which allows you to provision additional storage automatically when required.
Like EC2 instances, you must deploy your Amazon RDS databases in a VPC. This ensures that
you can configure your database with the necessary network security settings to allow access
only to authorized idx_9a2b35b6 resources.
The following section explains some best practices to consider when deploying your Amazon
RDS database.
Deploying an Amazon RDS database instance in a VPC
In most cases, you idx_1681a5ed should deploy idx_3fee676d your database in private subnets within your VPC, as they are
likely to contain sensitive data that must only be accessed by authorized applications. Placing
databases in public subnets is rarely necessary and poses a significant security risk.
Using a VPC allows you to configure various network security components, ensuring that only
specific applications running on other AWS resources can directly connect to the database.
Refer to the architectural diagram in Figure 9.6. Belly Brew Co. Limited's application is
deployed on EC2 instances within the App Subnets. This application needs to connect to the
backend database, which is deployed in the Data Subnet, also a private subnet.
◦
•
Amazon RDS Storage Autoscaling automatically increases database storage when
required, up to a maximum limit that you define. Storage can only scale up; once
additional storage has been allocated, it cannot be reduced without migrating to a new
database instance.
Note
251 Databases on AWS
Figure 9.6: Deploying Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance in VPC
As depicted in Figure 9.6, EC2 instances hosted in the App Subnets (private subnets) need to
connect to the idx_e4dcf74e MySQL database idx_7dbf7ec4 instances deployed in Amazon RDS. To enable this
connectivity, the security group attached to the database instances, Data-SG, permits inbound
traffic on port 3306, which is the default port for MySQL. The source of this traffic is restricted
to any instance associated with the App-SG security group. This ensures that only resources

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 250
chunks.content:
related to the App-SG are allowed to send traffic to the MySQL database instances.
You will notice that only a single database instance has been configured in this VPC. This is
because, with relational databases, there can only be one primary (or master) instance that is
both writable and readable. However, this setup can act as a single point of failure. If the
database instance idx_c1738ca6 fails, you idx_bc55dccd may lose all your data. That's where AWS backup and recovery
options come into play, which is the topic of the next section.
Backup and recovery
Your database is one of idx_1d97b84a the most critical elements of your application — it hosts valuable data
that your business depends on. AWS enables you to recover from the loss of any resource that
hosts this data, such as your database instance, by allowing you to back up critical data and
store that backup securely. In the event of a disaster, you can recover from the backup and
launch new RDS database instances, minimizing the loss incurred.

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 252
chunks.content:
Chapter 9 252
However, backups are typically performed at regular intervals, such as every four hours or
daily. Determining how often you should back up your data requires an understanding of your
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO).
These two parameters will help you design a recovery strategy that meets your business
requirements:
RTO: This represents idx_0c5c0b52 the amount of time (in hours) it takes to recover from a disaster
and return to a working state. The recovery time includes provisioning a new database
instance and performing a restore operation, which depends on the volume of data
being restored.
RPO: This defines the idx_0eb7f687 amount of data (measured as a factor of time) you are willing to
lose in the event of a disaster. For example, if you cannot afford to lose more than four
hours of data, then you must back up your data at least every four hours. The shorter
the RPO, the less data is at risk of being lost during a failure.
Based on your RTO and RPO requirements, you can define your backup strategy. Amazon RDS
offers two types of backup options: automatic backups and manual snapshots.
Automatic backups are generated idx_427a1fdd and managed by AWS. When enabled, these
backups occur daily, and AWS provides a maximum retention period of 35 days. You
can configure the retention period between 1 and 35 days. Older backups are
automatically deleted after the set retention period. You can restore your database from
these automatic backups at any time within the retention window. When you delete
your database, AWS automatically deletes the associated automatic backups.
Manual snapshots require you to initiate the backup manually. You should do this
before making a significant change to your application or database, so you have a
recent backup to revert to in case of failure. Unlike automatic backups, manual
snapshots are not automatically deleted — you must manually delete them when they
are no longer needed. Additionally, backups can be copied across AWS regions,
allowing you to restore a copy of your database in another region if necessary.
AWS stores backups of your database in Amazon S3. You do not have direct access to these
buckets. Instead, you must perform a restore operation from Amazon RDS to restore from
backups.
While backups and restores enable you to recover from disasters such as a database instance
failure, they do not provide high availability. Restoring a backup can take time, depending on
the size of the database, which may result in your customers being unable to access the
application until the restore process is fully complete. To address this limitation, AWS offers a
feature known as multi-AZ deployments, which is idx_dabf5c1e discussed in the next section.
•
•
•
•
253 Databases on AWS

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 252
chunks.content:
Amazon RDS multi-AZ options
When you idx_a92d1a33 deploy an idx_c105574f Amazon RDS database, you can deploy a single instance in a specific
subnet, which means that the instance resides in a single availability zone. Now, while backups
and restore operations can help you recover from disasters, they don't offer instant failover
capabilities in the event of a database instance failure or an availability zone outage.
Amazon RDS idx_0660f033 offers a feature idx_1bec51d5 known as multi-AZ, which involves having a primary instance of
your database in one availability zone and one or two standby copies of the database in
another idx_31327932 availability zone. Data from the primary instance is replicated to the standby copy.
AWS offers two options for configuring your RDS database with multi-AZ as follows:
Multi-AZ DB instance deployment
In a multi-AZ DB instance idx_66667ee8 deployment, you have one primary database instance that handles all
read and write requests. Resources such as EC2 instances must access this primary instance to
perform read or write operations. This instance is deployed in a specific subnet within an
Availability Zone. A standby copy of the database is automatically deployed in a different
Availability Zone, and data is synchronously replicated from the primary to the standby instance
as depicted in Figure 9.7:
Figure 9.7: Amazon RDS multi-AZ instance deployment
The standby instance idx_c428e05d is not accessible when a multi-AZ instance idx_117499f3 configuration is in use. In the
event of a failure of the primary instance, AWS automatically initiates a failover to the standby

which is promoted to become the new primary instance. A new standby instance replaces the

Since connectivity to the database is managed using a DNS endpoint, AWS handles the backend
redirection to the new IP address during failover. This means you do not need to reconfigure your
applications after a failover.
Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment
Amazon RDS also idx_d30b3afe offers the Multi-AZ DB Cluster deployment feature, which provides
additional capabilities compared to the Multi-AZ instance deployment option. In this
configuration, replication is semi-synchronous —meaning the primary DB instance waits for
at least one replica (not necessarily all) to acknowledge receipt of the data, though not
necessarily confirmation of durability (i.e., writing the data to disk). This approach improves idx_725a23f5
durability over asynchronous replication while reducing the performance impact typically
associated with fully synchronous replication.
According to the diagram in Figure 9.8, the Multi-AZ DB Cluster deployment consists of two
read-replica DB instances, in addition to the primary writeable DB instance.
Figure 9.8: Amazon RDS multi-AZ DB cluster
255 Databases on AWS
These three instances are distributed across three separate Availability Zones, providing high
availability, increased read capacity, and lower write latency compared to the multi-AZ DB
instance deployment.
Amazon RDS offers a single writable instance of your database by default. This means that the
primary master copy of the database must be online and accessible to commit any write
operations. As a Cloud Practitioner, you must consider how well your database can scale to
handle increasing idx_945ae457 load. For relational databases, such as Amazon RDS, running idx_1d5627ff engines like
MySQL or PostgreSQL, you can only scale out your read requests using a feature known as read
replicas. This is discussed in the next section.
Amazon RDS read replicas
An Amazon RDS Read Replica is idx_25ac5128 a read-only copy of a database that applications can use to
perform read queries. The replica is created by taking a snapshot of the primary instance and
launching a new read-only instance from that snapshot. Asynchronous replication from the
primary database to the read replica ensures that data changes committed to the primary
instance are eventually reflected on the replica.
This setup reduces the load on the primary database by offloading read traffic to the replicas. It
also enables continued support for read queries during planned maintenance on the primary
instance.
As shown in Figure 9.9, you can create multiple read replicas from a single primary DB instance,
allowing you to scale out your read workloads to meet increasing demand.

against data corruption—any corruption on the primary is likely replicated to the
standby. Regular backups, whether automated or manual, are essential, especially
before making changes. Using both multi-AZ and backups ensures greater data
protection and recovery options.

As shown in Figure 9.9, you can also create idx_de0517ce read replicas of your database instance in other

from a primary instance located in the London region. This configuration is useful for disaster

In the event of a major disaster, a read replica can be promoted to function as a standalone
primary database instance. This promotion severs the replication link to the original primary
instance, effectively creating a new independent master database.
In addition to the standard open source and third-party engines offered by Amazon RDS, you
also have Amazon Aurora, which is AWS's proprietary database engine that is compatible with
MySQL and idx_b4ee60cf PostgreSQL engines. A brief overview of Amazon Aurora is provided in the next
section.
Introduction to Amazon Aurora
Amazon Aurora is AWS's proprietary MySQL-compatible and PostgreSQL-compatible
relational database service, designed idx_a9f769c7 for enterprise-grade workloads and production
environments. It offers a comprehensive set of features, including high availability, automatic
healing, and seamless scalability, to meet diverse business requirements. It is designed to be up
to five times faster than standard MySQL and up to three times faster than PostgreSQL.
257 Databases on AWS
Aurora achieves these capabilities through its unique architecture, which automatically
replicates data across a minimum of three Availability Zones. The architecture is depicted in
the following diagram in Figure 9.10. You will note that the Aurora service provisions instances
and a shared cluster volume across three availability zones.
Figure 9.10: AWS Aurora DB cluster
Aurora offers built-in fault tolerance and supports up to 15 low-latency read replicas to
efficiently scale read-intensive workloads. These read replicas not only help scale read
operations but also provide multi-AZ capabilities. In the event of a failure of the primary
instance, Aurora can idx_c967495c instantly fail over to one of the read replicas. Unlike standard Amazon
RDS, which uses EBS volumes attached to specific database instances, Aurora uses a shared
storage architecture. It supports up to 128 TiB of storage per database and includes an auto-
healing feature. Amazon Aurora is provisioned as a database cluster, which is discussed in the
next section.
Amazon Aurora DB clusters
When launching an idx_17b42b7e Amazon Aurora database, you provision a DB cluster that idx_aa68db30 consists of one
or more DB instances and a cluster volume. This cluster volume spans multiple Availability
Zones and hosts copies of the cluster data.

The DB cluster is composed of two types of DB instances:
Primary DB instance: Supports both read and write operations and performs all data
modifications to the cluster volume. The primary instance is accessible via the cluster
endpoint.
Aurora Replicas: You can create up to 15 Aurora Replicas in addition to the primary
instance. Although these replicas connect to the same cluster volume, they are used
only for read operations. Applications can connect to them via the reader endpoint.
Aurora Replicas are designed to handle read queries and can also be used for failover if the
primary instance fails.
When provisioning Amazon Aurora, you must select a DB instance class, which can be either
burstable or memory-optimized, with various instance types offering different levels of CPU,
memory, and idx_d56ee303 network idx_47ba74db capacity. Additionally, Amazon Aurora is also available as a serverless
option, which is discussed in the next section.
Amazon Aurora Serverless
Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 is a fully managed service that includes built-in autoscaling
capabilities, allowing it to idx_6a95d542 automatically adjust database capacity based on workload patterns
and application demand. You are charged only for the resources consumed by your DB cluster,
helping you avoid overprovisioning unless explicitly required by your application.
You do not need to specify the instance class, type, or size for your Aurora Serverless database.
Instead, you define Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs), which Amazon Aurora uses to provision the
required capacity. Each ACU provides approximately 2 GiB of memory along with a
corresponding amount of CPU and network bandwidth. You specify a minimum and maximum
number of ACUs for your cluster, and Amazon Aurora will scale within this range—adding or
removing capacity based on application load.
Interestingly, the ACU count can scale down to zero, allowing the cluster to pause after a
period of inactivity. This can be highly cost-efficient, as when your cluster is paused, you are
only charged for the storage consumed.
Aurora Serverless is ideal for development and testing environments, as well as production
workloads with unpredictable usage patterns. For example, an e-commerce website might
experience increased traffic during the winter or rainy seasons. Another use case is deploying a
new web application when its popularity is still uncertain. Once usage trends are clearer, you
can decide whether to transition to a standard Aurora deployment or continue using the
serverless architecture.

Relational databases, also known as SQL databases, are designed to help you build an array of
related tables idx_1b02fa94 with idx_188d3509 complex joins, enabling efficient and powerful queries. However, they
require that data be stored in a structured format with a strictly defined schema.
The schema refers to the idx_9b2bdf9a table structure consisting of rows and columns, where rows represent
individual items and columns represent attributes whose values provide context to those
items. In most cases, this schema must be defined at the outset, and making changes to it later
can be challenging. Additionally, all data must conform to this structured format.
Relational databases, such as Amazon RDS, also have specific performance limitations,
particularly when handling highly scalable or high-throughput workloads.
To address such use cases, AWS offers other database options, including NoSQL (Non-
Relational) databases idx_fe3b2801 like Amazon DynamoDB. DynamoDB stores idx_d4a12276 data as key-value pairs in
JSON document format, and it does not require a strict, predefined schema.
The following section provides a high-level overview of Amazon DynamoDB.
Using Amazon DynamoDB for NoSQL workloads
Amazon DynamoDB idx_61d5d82b is AWS's NoSQL, non-relational idx_e0a7eebd database solution, capable of delivering
single-digit millisecond latency. The service operates from within the AWS public space, so you
do not need to place instances in your VPC. Your compute resources can connect to DynamoDB
tables by making API calls to the database.
Thanks to its serverless architecture, there is no need to specify instance classes, types or sizes.
You also do not need to specify storage volume capacity. Instead, you define provisioned
capacity in terms idx_1ed8c4ea of read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs), which
idx_df374222 AWS uses to provision the necessary infrastructure. Alternatively, you can opt for on-demand

data is stored on solid-state drives (SSDs), and the idx_1c6fa057 underlying storage is replicated across
multiple Availability Zones, ensuring durability and availability.
NoSQL databases, such as DynamoDB, support both semi-structured and structured data,
including key-value pairs and document data models defined in JSON (JavaScript Object
Notation) format. A fundamental idx_b6f9de08 difference between DynamoDB and Amazon RDS is that
with DynamoDB, you do not need to specify a strict schema. The schema can be modified on
the fly and updated as needed. Each item in a DynamoDB table does not require a value for
every attribute. To get started, you only need a primary key and, optionally, a sort key to
define the uniqueness of each item stored in the table.
AWS DynamoDB offers excellent performance and resilience features, making it ideal for
modern web-based and mobile applications. It is the database of choice for gaming, streaming,
and financial services applications. DynamoDB is well-suited for use cases with strict
availability requirements, eliminating the need for manual scaling of instances or storage
capacity.
Some key features of DynamoDB include:
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX): DAX is a fully managed caching feature that enhances
the idx_c2c5d320 performance of your DynamoDB tables. It significantly reduces response times
from milliseconds to microseconds for frequently accessed data. Unlike traditional
caching solutions, DAX is easy to configure and does not require your application to
manage both the cache and the database separately. This feature is particularly
effective for read-heavy or bursty workloads, designed for eventually consistent reads
and it minimizes the need to overprovision read capacity units.
DynamoDB Global Tables: This feature provides a fully managed, multi-region, and
multi-active idx_5bc05fad database architecture that enables you to localize read and write
operations. Global Tables allow you to deploy replicas of your table in multiple AWS
regions. Each application can write to its local copy, and data is automatically
replicated across regions to keep all tables in sync. This makes Global Tables ideal for
applications that require high availability and low-latency access across geographically
dispersed regions.
DynamoDB Streams: This feature idx_066538cc captures a time-ordered sequence of item-level
changes that occur in your DynamoDB tables. With Streams, you can view and react to
data modifications before the change, after the change, or both. DynamoDB Streams
stores recent changes to your items over a rolling 24-hour period. This enables you to
add real-time processing and additional intelligence to your application's business
